table_stats.source: pg_class.reltuples and pg_total_relation_size, exported from staging on 2026-11-10 (row counts only)

findings.statement: ALTER TABLE Plant ALTER COLUMN price TYPE DECIMAL(10,2) USING ROUND(price::numeric, 2)
findings.effect: On databases created before the squash, Plant.price is still DOUBLE PRECISION (prisma/migration_history_archive/20251001090000_init/migration.sql:15): the conversion rounds every price to 2 decimal places, and a value of 1e8 or more aborts the migration. On databases built from the baseline the column is already DECIMAL(10,2) and nothing changes, so the loss only shows on the older databases.

size.source: pg_class.reltuples and pg_total_relation_size, exported from staging on 2026-11-10 (row counts only)

findings.rewrite: Before converting, count the rows that would change (SELECT count(*) FROM "Plant" WHERE price::numeric <> round(price::numeric, 2) OR abs(price) >= 1e8) on each pre-squash database, copy price to a backup column, then convert; keep the backup until the totals reconcile
findings.verification: On a copy of a pre-squash database, run the count above, apply the migration, and compare sum(price) before and after

findings.statement: ALTER TABLE Plant ALTER COLUMN weight_kg TYPE DECIMAL(8,3) USING ROUND(weight_kg::numeric, 3)
findings.effect: On pre-squash databases weight_kg is DOUBLE PRECISION (archive init migration line 16): weights are rounded to the gram, and a weight of 100 000 kg or more aborts the migration

findings.statement: ALTER TABLE "Order" ALTER COLUMN "total" TYPE DECIMAL(10,2) USING ROUND("total"::numeric, 2)
findings.effect: On pre-squash databases Order.total is DOUBLE PRECISION (prisma/migration_history_archive/20251110090000_orders/migration.sql:6): 2.6 million order totals are rounded to the cent, so stored totals can differ from what was charged, and any total of 1e8 or more aborts the migration

findings.rewrite: Add total_cents BIGINT, backfill it in batches from round(total * 100) after reconciling the rows that change, switch reads, and drop total in a later release

findings.statement: ALTER TABLE Order ADD COLUMN channel TEXT NOT NULL
findings.effect: Order.channel is added NOT NULL with no default. On a table with rows PostgreSQL refuses the ADD COLUMN, so the migration fails; and if it did apply, placeOrder() (src/orders.ts:4) still creates orders without channel during the rolling deploy. importOrder() passes a variable as data and could not be checked; the test in tests/orders.test.ts also omits it

findings.statement: ALTER TABLE "Order" ALTER COLUMN "total" TYPE DECIMAL(10,2) USING ROUND("total"::numeric, 2)
findings.engine_range: postgresql: all versions (most type changes rewrite)
findings.effect: The USING clause rewrites all of Order (2.6 million rows, 1.4 GB) under ACCESS EXCLUSIVE, even on databases where total is already DECIMAL(10,2); Prisma sends the file as one transaction, so the lock is held until the last statement commits

findings.rewrite: Only convert where the column is still DOUBLE PRECISION (a DO block that checks information_schema.columns), or use the add-backfill-switch sequence of F03
findings.verification: On a copy with production-size data, time the statement and watch pg_locks for the ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock

findings.effect: The index is built inside a DO block, so no rule saw it: CREATE INDEX without CONCURRENTLY holds a SHARE lock on Order (2.6 million rows) and blocks every insert and update until it is built, and inside Prisma's transaction until the migration commits

findings.rewrite: Move the index to its own migration containing only CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS "Order_createdAt_idx" ON "Order" ("createdAt"); (Prisma runs a migration with a single CONCURRENTLY statement outside a transaction)
findings.verification: Apply on a copy and check pg_locks during the build: only SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE should appear

findings.statement: ALTER TABLE "Order" ALTER COLUMN "total" TYPE DECIMAL(10,2) USING ROUND("total"::numeric, 2)
findings.effect: Nothing sets lock_timeout: if a long report holds Order or Customer when the migration starts, the ALTER waits and every later query on the table queues behind it

steps: On each pre-squash database, count the price, weight and total values the conversion would change, and back the columns up
SET lock_timeout and statement_timeout at the top of each migration (F10)
Plant conversion in its own migration, guarded to run only where the column is DOUBLE PRECISION (F01, F02, F11)
StockAlert table, its index and foreign key as written
ADD COLUMN channel TEXT DEFAULT 'web' and giftNote (F04)
Code sets channel, writes mobile and phone, writes total_cents (F04, F05)
Batched backfill of mobile and total_cents (F03, F08)
channel SET NOT NULL through a validated CHECK
Drop phone, total and legacy_ref after exporting legacy_ref (F06)

headline.statement: Do not deploy 20260415000000_release_hardening as written. On databases created before the squash it rounds every price, weight and order total stored as DOUBLE PRECISION, it cannot add Order.channel to a table with rows, and the running code still reads phone and legacy_ref. The index in its DO block and the Order rewrite lock a 2.6 million row table for the rest of the migration.
headline.scope_statement: Static review of the one pending Prisma migration and src/ against PostgreSQL 16.4 as the docker-compose file assumes (the production version is not in the repository), with staging row counts and the archived pre-squash history. Durations and locks were not measured, schema drift was not checked, and no other service was searched.

limitations: The dynamic check did not run (no Docker, Podman or loopback PostgreSQL), so no finding is measured.
The engine version comes from the development docker-compose file; findings that depend on it are assumed and capped at P1.
Which production databases predate the squash is not in the repository; the narrowing findings hold for those.
importOrder() passes a variable as Prisma data, so whether it sets channel could not be read.
Squawk was not installed; only the built-in rules and a reading of the DO block ran.
